hook: "Scripted founder ads have been on a consistent blind spot among consumers"
body: Kanish Digital argues scripted founder ads are a consumer blind spot, while unscripted founder ads about ONE thing the product does well have taken over the format and work well.
idea: One unscripted thing beats one scripted everything — specificity is what makes founder ads work.
sequencing: The blind-spot claim: scripted founder ads get tuned out by consumers.
The takeover: unscripted ads about ONE thing the product does well.
The verdict: it works well.
The link as the implied evidence.
formatting: Single-line X post with a link attachment.
why_it_works: Specificity reads as honesty; a script read to camera reads as an ad.
what_to_steal: LC founder ads should each cover ONE thing (waterproof, tarnish-free, stackable) — never the whole catalog in one ad.

hook: "my magnesium is better than your magnesium : most convincing founder ads"
body: A one-liner praising an unnamed magnesium brand's founder ads as the most convincing, built on the 'my magnesium is better than your magnesium' challenge framing.
idea: The most convincing founder ad is a direct 'mine beats yours' challenge issued by the founder personally.
sequencing: The claim: most convincing founder ads.
The mechanism named: 'my magnesium is better than your magnesium.'

The wager: the founder's own name behind the claim.

what_to_steal: LC's head-to-head: 'my waterproof jewelry vs your green-skin jewelry,' said by Jay on camera.

hook: "If you haven't tested these ad formats yet, you should:"
body: William Kast lists 5 formats to test: (1) founder talking head — raw, low production, 30 seconds of genuine talk outperforms polished content; (2) voiceless B-roll ads — B-roll plus text overlay bullets, clean and scalable; (3) yapper ads — uncut organic talking, trust faster than anything polished; (4) AI educational videos; (5) camouflage ads — native-looking image plus long-form emotional storytelling, people don't realize it's an ad until invested. Closes with: the format gets attention, the message gets the conversion.
idea: Raw founder talking-head is the first format to test — format gets attention, message gets conversion.
sequencing: Founder talking head: raw, 30s of genuine talk beats polished.
Voiceless B-roll: B-roll plus text overlay bullets, clean and scalable.
Yapper: uncut organic talking, trust faster than polished.
AI educational: for health brands that must educate before selling.
Camouflage: native image plus long emotional story; the ad-frame arrives late.
The reframe: the format gets attention, the message gets the conversion.
why_it_works: Raw talking head borrows the trust dynamics of a FaceTime call — low production IS the production.
what_to_steal: The '30 seconds of genuine talk outperforms polished content' rule for LC founder clips.

idea: The bar for founder ads is 'organic yet explanatory' — native feel plus clear teaching.
sequencing: The praise: genuinely liking @myfrido's founder ads.
Quality one: organic — they don't feel like ads.
Quality two: explanatory — they still teach.
The heart emoji as the viewer's verdict.
why_it_works: Viewers reward ads that feel like content but teach like ads — the praise names exactly that combination.
what_to_steal: LC's quality bar for founder ads: native feel, one clear explanation per ad.

sequencing: Headline promise: 30 scroll-stopping formats.
Hooks folder: 6 hook types.
Founder Content folder: intro, journey→result, 'I wish I knew earlier', walking monologue, car monologue, whiteboard explainer.
Social Proof, Educational, Entertainment, Creative, and Bonus folders complete the tree.
formatting: X text post with an ASCII folder-tree.
why_it_works: Naming the sub-formats makes founder content testable instead of vibes-based.
what_to_steal: The 6-way split for LC: shoot each founder sub-format (walk, car, whiteboard, journey→result) against the same winning message.

hook: "We've scaled accounts to $30k/day on 3-4 core angles."

Very authentic and impossible to copy. The founder will always convey most conviction.' The secret is lots of ad formats, not lots of angles.
idea: Scale comes from repackaging few angles into many formats — founder ads are the moat because conviction can't be copied.

The secret: lots of ad formats, not lots of angles.
Founders Ads ranked #1: authentic, impossible to copy, most conviction.
The remaining 14 formats as repackaging options.
The payoff: one message, many formats.

what_to_steal: Jay on camera is LC's uncopyable asset: competitors can clone the statics, not the founder's face.

hook: "Ad formats that are dead in 2026:"
body: Adam Taylor lists ad formats dead in 2026 — polished studio product videos, 'hey guys' UGC intros, discount-led statics, founder story VSLs — versus formats printing money: ugly advertorial statics, long-form yapper ads, comment-reply UGC hooks, us-vs-them comparison statics. Closes with: the format is never the biggest lever; the angle underneath it is.
idea: Long founder-story VSLs are dead; raw long-form yapper is the living version — and angle beats format anyway.
sequencing: The dead list: polished studio, 'hey guys' UGC, discount statics, founder-story VSLs.
The printing list: ugly advertorial statics, long-form yapper, comment-reply hooks, us-vs-them statics.
The reframe: the angle underneath is the biggest lever.
The implication for founder ads: the story survives, the polish dies.
why_it_works: The same founder story dies polished and lives raw — production value is the variable, not the story.
what_to_steal: Kill LC's polished founder VSLs; reshoot the same stories as uncut yapper clips.

hook: "Your Founder Is Your Startup's Most Underrated Marketing Asset"
body: Seun Olasunkanmi's long-form argument that the founder is a startup's most underrated marketing asset: people are increasingly interested in the people behind companies. A company post ('We're excited to announce our latest product update') loses to a founder post ('We spent three months building this feature. Then customers told us we were solving the wrong problem. Here's what happened next') because the founder version creates curiosity, story, and connection. Includes a 5-theme founder content strategy: founder lessons, customer problems, building the company, industry opinions, product stories.
idea: The founder's story, experience, and thinking are a marketing asset most founders leave dormant.
sequencing: The thesis: the founder is the most underrated marketing asset.
The shift: people care about the people behind companies, not just the product.
The comparison: company post vs founder post — curiosity, story, connection.
The audience's real questions: why did you start, what did you learn, what do you believe.
The 5-theme strategy: founder lessons, customer problems, building the company, industry opinions, product stories.
why_it_works: A founder's thinking is scarce and non-commoditizable — it's the only content competitors can't replicate.
what_to_steal: The 5-theme map as LC's founder content calendar: lessons, customer problems, building, opinions, product stories.

The ripping format is 'Founder ads' — a walk and talk about YOUR brand. CTA is aimed at NYC CPG founders to DM him.
cta: "DM me and we'll make some banger ads together" (agency pitch)
idea: The founder walk-and-talk interview is a productized ad format — 105 interviews in 16 weeks proves the machine.
sequencing: The volume proof: 105 founder interviews in 16 weeks.
The names: SolidCore, Venmo, Promix, Bloom, Cuts, Hampton, Tony Robbins family office.
The format: 'Founder ads' — a walk and talk about YOUR brand.
The claim: your founder story is what customers want to hear.
The pitch: NYC CPG founders, DM me.
why_it_works: The interview format outsources authenticity — the host's questions make the founder's story feel discovered, not pitched.
what_to_steal: The interview dynamic: have someone interview Jay while walking — the Q&A rhythm beats a solo monologue.

The prescription: spend days making more of what rips.

what_to_steal: LC's creative rule: double down on proven founder ads before testing new AI formats.

hook: "You don't need to become more interesting to build a personal brand."
body: Degensing's founder-story framework: you don't need to be more interesting, you need to pay attention to what already happened to you (the customer conversation that changed your mind, the product you killed, the hire you got wrong, the costly mistake). Most founders tell the story without extracting the thinking. The framework: Story → Tension → Insight → Point of view, with a 5-question test (did something change, was there a decision, was something at stake, did you learn, does it reveal how you think). 15 prompts live in a free playbook.
cta: Comment "STORY" for the free Founder Personal Brand Playbook.
idea: Founder content works when the story extracts the thinking — Story → Tension → Insight → Point of view.
sequencing: The reframe: pay attention to what already happened, don't manufacture interestingness.
The raw material: customer conversations, killed products, bad hires, costly mistakes.
The mistake: telling the story without extracting the thinking.
The example rewrite: feature flop → the real, uncomfortable lesson.
The framework: Story → Tension → Insight → Point of view.
The 5-question test for any story.
The playbook CTA: comment 'STORY'.
formatting: Long X post with a photo; comment-gated lead magnet.
why_it_works: Stories are memorable but thinking is persuasive — the framework turns anecdotes into authority.
what_to_steal: Run every LC founder story through the 5-question test before shooting.

what_to_steal: LC shouldn't let imperfect delivery block shooting — a script-read founder ad can still run 9 months.

hook: "How Personal Should a Founder Brand Get?"
body: Degensing's boundaries framework for founder brands: reject 'be authentic, share everything.' The filter is 'does sharing this help people understand how I think.' Green (share freely): business lessons, customer insights, mistakes, principles. Yellow (share carefully): difficult periods, financial pressure, family-involved experiences. Red (keep private): family privacy, confidential info, unresolved conflicts.
idea: Founder authenticity needs boundaries — share what reveals your thinking, not your diary.
sequencing: The question: how personal should a founder brand get.
Reject the bad advice: 'be authentic, share everything.'
The real filter: does it help people understand how you think.
Green list: lessons, insights, decisions, mistakes, principles.
Yellow list: difficult periods, pressure, family-involved experiences.
Red list: privacy, confidentials, unresolved conflicts.
The rule: personal enough to be human, not a diary.
formatting: Long X post with green/yellow/red emoji coding.
why_it_works: Bounded vulnerability builds trust; unbounded oversharing builds discomfort.
what_to_steal: LC's founder-content filter: every Jay story must pass 'does this reveal how I think?' before it ships.

hook: "the 5 ad creative formats that convert highest in dropshipping right now ranked by performance:"
body: Alex Page's ranked list of the 5 highest-converting dropship formats: (1) UGC problem/solution, (2) 'TikTok made me buy it', (3) us-vs-them split screen, (4) founder/operator talking head — 'I designed this because I was tired of [problem]'; converts lower on first view but retargets at 2-3x because the face creates familiarity ('the face IS the retargeting; people remember faces not products'), (5) text-overlay slideshow. Common thread: they feel native; the best ad doesn't look like an ad.
idea: The founder's face is a retargeting asset — lower first-view conversion, 2–3x retargeting, because people remember faces, not products.
sequencing: #1 UGC problem/solution: friend-recommendation feel, unpolished converts.
#2 'TikTok made me buy it': fast cuts, social proof built into the format.
#3 us-vs-them: split screen, visual conflict, highest CTR.
#4 founder talking head: 'I designed this because...' — the face IS the retargeting.
#5 slideshow with text overlays: problem→solution→proof→offer, 15 minutes to make.
The common thread: native feel; the best ad doesn't look like an ad.
why_it_works: Faces create familiarity across exposures — the founder becomes the brand's memory hook.
what_to_steal: Deploy LC founder talking-heads primarily as retargeting (MOF/BOF), not prospecting — Jay's face is the memory hook.

hook: "This Eskiin ad is by far one of the best founder-led DTC ads I've seen lately." (The ad itself opens on the vision board: a 16-year-old kid, one goal — retire his mom.)
body: Luis Felipe's breakdown of an Eskiin filtered-showerhead founder ad (235s mini-VSL, full transcript included): it opens with a vision board — a 16-year-old kid, one goal: retire his mom (open loop: how did he do it?). Then personal story (eczema, dry skin, hair loss, rashes) → failed solutions (medications, shampoos, treatments) → the reframe ('Could it be our water?') → mechanism (chlorine, heavy metals, contaminants in tap water) → the product built as the answer (better filtration, strong pressure, clean design) → mission zoom-out (American fulfillment, no dropshipping, customer service) → customer proof (mom approved, half a million customers) → emotional payoff (December 2024: they retired their mom) → 100% money-back guarantee + CTA to try Eskiin.
cta: "we would love for you to try Eskiin" backed by a 100% money-back guarantee.
idea: The founder story IS the sales argument — personal story → failed solutions → new mechanism → product as logical conclusion → mission → emotional payoff.
sequencing: Vision-board open loop: a 16-year-old kid, one goal — retire his mom. How did he do it.
Personal story: chronic eczema, dry skin, hair loss in clumps, mystery rashes.
Failed solutions: medications, shampoos, treatments — nothing works.
The reframe: 'Could it be our water?' — a new explanation for an old problem.
Mechanism: chlorine, heavy metals, pesticides, mold in tap water; the shower as chemical exposure zone.
The product as logical conclusion: built to fix everything hated about alternatives — filtration, pressure, design.
Mission zoom-out plus proof: American fulfillment, no dropshipping, customer service; mom obsessed, half a million customers.
Emotional payoff then guarantee + CTA: December 2024 — they retired their mom; 100% money-back, 'try Eskiin' — only after earning the emotional investment.
formatting: 235s video ad (amplify thumbnail) with a full auto-transcript; a mini-VSL disguised as a founder story.
why_it_works: The ad earns the right to sell by making you care about two brothers first — the product becomes the logical conclusion of a story, not a pitch.
what_to_steal: The open-loop structure for LC: Jay's personal jewelry problem (tarnish/green skin) → failed solutions → the waterproof mechanism → mission → payoff.

hook: "🔥 This founder ad shows the founder for six seconds." (The ad opens: 'Mouth taping sounds dangerous until you actually understand what it does to your sleep.')
body: Mighty King breaks down a mouth tape brand's founder ad that ran 251 days: the founder appears for only six seconds, opening with 'Mouth taping sounds dangerous until you actually understand what it does to your sleep.'
